crossrefs.text: Then the LordGod formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.

Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil. He still retains his integrity, even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause.”
Will you speak wickedly on Godʼs behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Then Jobʼs wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.

Although they may fast, I will not listen to their cry; although they may offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will finish them off by sword and famine and plague.”
Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.
Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.
There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his childrenʼs children, but the sinnerʼs wealth is passed to the righteous.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spiderʼs web.
He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.
Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
On the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their portion.
His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
